title: KP2PLab Experiment Analysis
description: Analyze session-window conditional delivery bounds, starting-cohort delivery and coverage, measurement uncertainty, first on-time stable remote latency, observed duplicates, GossipSub wire control traffic, churn, and network conditions.

options.content: **Choose Run, Agent and Topic, then a time range.** Traffic uses rate/increase. **Session-window cards use the whole observed run and only Run.** Stable delivery requires subscription throughout each fixed window (default 10s); departures are excluded even after early success. Known starting-cohort delivery retains departures. Read both bounds with coverage, availability-unknown, incomplete-measurement, and pending counts. Bounds are not confidence intervals and describe only receiver sessions whose presence at publication is proven. Late telemetry can revise results; clocks must be synchronized. Completely invisible telemetry cannot be detected. Legacy publications are reported separately and excluded from new metrics.

panels.title: Online Agents
panels.description: Current online hosts matching the Agent filter. The Run and Topic filters do not affect this panel.

panels.title: Ready Peers
panels.description: Current ready Peers for the selected runs and Agents. Ready does not guarantee a stable mesh. Zero is shown only when Peers in another state have been observed for the selected runs and Agents. If the selection has no observations, it remains No observations.

panels.title: Published · Total
panels.description: Sum of publish counters currently retained by the collector. This is not the increase over the selected time range, and it may reset when the collector restarts.

panels.title: Published · Selected range
panels.description: Estimated increase in published messages over the selected time range. Prometheus increase accounts for interval boundaries and counter resets, so the result may not be an integer.

panels.title: Failures · Selected range
panels.description: Estimated increase in publish/leave failures handled with onError: continue over the selected time range. Failures that stop a run with onError: fail and join failures are not included. Also check for failed runs in the Run status and phase panel.

panels.title: Telemetry loss · Range
panels.description: Events reported as lost in the telemetry pipeline during the selected time range. This is separate from P2P packet loss and affects the completeness of the analysis.

panels.title: Stable delivery · Bounds
panels.description: session-window-v1: on-time successful pairs among instrumented receiver sessions proven subscribed throughout the fixed window. A pre-deadline departure is excluded even after early receipt. Lower=S/E; upper=(S+unknown)/E. These are missing-observation bounds, not confidence intervals or a claim about invisible sessions. Availability uncertainty is reported separately. Only the Run filter applies. Counts cover mature messages in the whole observed run unless stated otherwise; legacy publications are excluded.

panels.title: Starting cohort · Bounds
panels.description: On-time success among the known starting cohort: sessions proven present at actual publication time, including confirmed later departures and their early receipts. Pair-weighted across selected new runs. Bounds reflect unknown receipt evidence within that known cohort and remain available despite separately reported candidate-availability or measurement uncertainty. N/A only when there are no known starting pairs. This is not an estimate for unobserved candidates. Only the Run filter applies. Counts cover mature messages in the whole observed run unless stated otherwise; legacy publications are excluded.

panels.title: Stable coverage
panels.description: Bounds on stable coverage within the known starting cohort. Lower = proven stable / known starting pairs. Upper additionally treats continuity-unknown known starting pairs as stable. Confirmed departures remain outside both numerators. Candidate sessions whose presence at publication is unknown are reported separately and do not enter this conditional denominator. N/A only when there are no known starting pairs. Network disconnection and mesh removal do not exclude subscribers. Only the Run filter applies. Counts cover mature messages in the whole observed run unless stated otherwise; legacy publications are excluded.

panels.title: Stable receiver pairs
panels.description: Receiver-session pairs proven subscribed from publication through its deadline. Zero pairs means the delivery ratio is N/A, not 0% or 100%. This is a sum across messages, not a distinct Peer count. Only the Run filter applies. Counts cover mature messages in the whole observed run unless stated otherwise; legacy publications are excluded.

panels.title: Starting-cohort pairs
panels.description: Recorded receiver-session pairs proven present at actual publication time. Confirmed departures stay in this count. Availability-unknown candidates are reported separately: this observed count is not a claim that the entire population was seen. Only the Run filter applies. Counts cover mature messages in the whole observed run unless stated otherwise; legacy publications are excluded.

panels.title: Avg duplicates / reached pair
panels.description: Observed extra PubSub copies within the delivery window at stable on-time successful remote pairs, divided by those successful pairs. Missing copy telemetry can lower the average. Not TCP retransmissions, duplicate bytes, or copies per publication. Only the Run filter applies. Counts cover mature messages in the whole observed run unless stated otherwise; legacy publications are excluded.

panels.title: Stable receipt outcomes
panels.description: Unknown: no on-time receipt and an incomplete source sequence prefix or invalid timestamp ordering. Missed: no on-time receipt with complete relevant source evidence. Late: first receipt after the deadline; a late pair can also be a miss. These categories must not be added as disjoint totals. Only the Run filter applies. Counts cover mature messages in the whole observed run unless stated otherwise; legacy publications are excluded.

panels.title: Availability unknown pairs
panels.description: Candidate uncertainty split by stage. Publication availability unknown means presence at publication was not proven, so the pair is outside the known starting cohort. Continuity unknown means presence at publication was proven, but neither survival through the deadline nor an earlier departure was established. Total is their compatibility sum. These are not confirmed departures or packet loss and do not suppress conditional known-cohort bounds. Only the Run filter applies. Counts cover mature messages in the whole observed run unless stated otherwise; legacy publications are excluded.

panels.title: Message windows
panels.description: Pending publications have not reached their deadline and do not enter finalized pair totals. Finalized means the window has elapsed; later telemetry can still correct its result. A 2-second checkpoint period does not extend the deadline. Only the Run filter applies. Counts cover mature messages in the whole observed run unless stated otherwise; legacy publications are excluded.

panels.title: Departed receiver pairs
panels.description: Sessions proven present at publication and confirmed stopped before its deadline. Both early successful and unsuccessful departures are excluded from the stable cohort, but retained in starting-cohort counts. Agent termination is an end-time upper bound, not a receipt checkpoint. Only the Run filter applies. Counts cover mature messages in the whole observed run unless stated otherwise; legacy publications are excluded.

panels.title: Incomplete new runs
panels.description: Number of selected new runs with known unscoped measurement streams. This is an independent data-quality warning; known starting-cohort ratios and coverage remain available when their denominator exists. Zero cannot detect completely invisible telemetry or prove observation of every physical Peer. Only the Run filter applies. Counts cover mature messages in the whole observed run unless stated otherwise; legacy publications are excluded.

panels.title: Legacy publications excluded
panels.description: Publications from historical definitions, including dispatch-cohort-v1 without a fixed deadline. Raw logs remain available; no session evidence is invented. This panel also reports legacy-only runs, which provide no new window ratios. Only the Run filter applies. Counts include all observed historical publications, with no inferred delivery deadline.

panels.title: Peer states
panels.description: Peer counts by state at scrape time. Stopped and failed Peers are included while retained in experiment records. Zero is shown only when Peers in another state have been observed for the selected runs and Agents. If the selection has no observations, it remains No observations.

panels.title: Message events / sec
panels.description: Per-second rates of collected events. Delivery occurs at multiple Peers, so the delivery rate can exceed the publish rate. Do not interpret their ratio as message reachability.

panels.title: Published / delivered bytes per second
panels.description: Instrumented PubSub data bytes. Raw data equals payloadSize; envelopes include JSON metadata and base64 encoding. This does not include TCP/IP framing, retransmissions, or libp2p signatures.

panels.title: Stable on-time latency · Whole-run P50 / P95 / P99
panels.description: session-window-v1 first application delivery latency for mature, stable, on-time remote envelope pairs. Local/raw/late/departed/unknown/negative samples are excluded. Conditional on observed success, so read delivery bounds and coverage alongside it. Run, Agent and Topic filters apply. These cumulative bucket estimates describe the whole observed run, not the selected interval. Late batches can revise buckets: query directly, not with rate/increase. Synchronize clocks; positive offsets can remain undetected. Legacy histogram series are not included.

panels.title: Mesh changes per second
panels.description: GRAFT/PRUNE follow the selected Topic filter. remove_peer is a Peer-level event without a topic and is shown independently of that filter. This chart shows event rates, not current mesh degree.

panels.title: Operation failures per second
panels.description: Rate of publish/leave failures handled with onError: continue. Failures that stop an experiment are not included in this counter. Also check for failed runs in the Run status and phase panel.

panels.title: Telemetry events dropped per second
panels.description: Events reported as lost in the telemetry pipeline. Message and mesh-event rates may be incomplete during these intervals. This is not the P2P network packet-loss rate.

panels.title: PubSub bytes · Selected range
panels.description: Estimated increase in PubSub data bytes over the selected time range, grouped by direction and encoding. Interface framing and retransmissions are not included.

panels.title: Control RPCs per second
panels.description: RPCs containing each control type, split by local send, receive, or pre-send drop. One mixed RPC contributes once to every contained type, so summing control types is not a unique envelope count. The Topic filter does not apply.

panels.title: Control entries per second
panels.description: Protobuf control entries carried by observed RPCs. An RPC can carry multiple entries of one type. The Topic filter does not apply because IWANT and IDONTWANT have no wire topic and one RPC can span topics.

panels.title: Control references per second
panels.description: Message-ID occurrences in IHAVE, IWANT, and IDONTWANT plus peer-exchange records in PRUNE. Repeated IDs are counted repeatedly and are not delivered messages. The Topic filter does not apply.

panels.title: Configured base delay · Mean / min / max
panels.description: Mean, minimum, and maximum base delay configured for ready/starting Peers. These are not measured packet RTT or propagation latency. Scope identifies the traffic affected by the impairment.

panels.title: Configured packet loss · Mean
panels.description: Mean configured loss probability for ready/starting Peers. This is not measured packet loss or the proportion of undelivered messages.

panels.title: Configured jitter · Mean
panels.description: Mean configured jitter for ready/starting Peers. Actual packet delay varies with the configured distribution; this value is not measured jitter.

panels.title: Peers with network configuration
panels.description: Ready/starting Peers included in network configuration metrics. Stopped and failed Peers are excluded.

panels.title: Agent capacity used
panels.description: Active Peer count divided by Agent capacity. This is not CPU or memory utilization. Agents with zero or unobserved capacity have no value.

panels.title: Time since last Agent report
panels.description: Elapsed time since the Agent last reported its status, not since the last Prometheus scrape. The Run and Topic filters do not affect this panel.

panels.title: KPL CPU by Agent
panels.description: Agent container plus owned running Peers, as a percentage of Docker host logical CPU capacity (whole host = 100%). Partial samples include measured containers only; compare container coverage. Missing host CPU counts produce no percentage.

panels.title: KPL memory by Agent
panels.description: Measured Agent and owned Peer containers: cgroup memory minus inactive file cache. Partial samples retain available memory without estimating missing containers. Compare container coverage.

panels.title: KPL total CPU
panels.description: Capacity-weighted CPU percentage for selected Agents with fresh samples and known host CPU counts. Whole combined host capacity = 100%. Partial samples are included without extrapolation. Standard deployment has one Agent per host.

panels.title: KPL total memory
panels.description: Sum of working sets for selected Agents with fresh samples, including partial samples. Missing container usage is not estimated; compare coverage.

panels.title: KPL resource measurement coverage
panels.description: Percentage of expected KPL containers successfully measured in a fresh online sample. For example, 46/47 is about 97.9%; CPU and memory still include those 46 containers. Offline/stale samples have zero measured containers.

panels.title: KPL memory including cache
panels.description: Raw summed cgroup memory usage including cache. Compare with working set; this is not a sum of container memory limits.

panels.title: Agent process CPU only
panels.description: Agent management process only, excluding Peers. CPU is normalized to Docker host logical CPU capacity (whole host = 100%). Requires a known host CPU count from a fresh KPL sample; raw process counters remain unchanged.

panels.title: Agent process resident memory only
panels.description: Agent management process RSS only; excludes Peer containers and differs from cgroup working set.

panels.title: Run status and phase
panels.description: Current state and phase number of selected runs. The Run filter applies; Agent and Topic filters do not.

panels.title: Experiment job states
panels.description: Current job counts by state for the selected runs, including terminal states such as completed, failed, and canceled.

panels.title: P2P stream throughput
panels.description: Latest source interval average, normally 5 seconds; stale non-final sessions disappear after 15 seconds. Closed sessions report zero. Run and Agent filters apply; Topic does not. Reported peers only. Excludes HTTP management and lower-layer wire overhead; not a capacity test.

panels.title: P2P stream throughput by protocol
panels.description: Negotiated stream protocol; empty protocol means negotiation/unassigned. Includes data forwarding and protocol control. Source monotonic interval averages, not telemetry arrival rates. Run and Agent filters apply.

panels.title: Cumulative P2P stream transfer
panels.description: Observed cumulative bytes, retaining final samples and separate process sessions in the current Controller lifetime. Saved-result analysis reconstructs history after a Controller restart. An unfinalized or completely missing session can undercount. Do not add send and receive as unique network bytes.

panels.title: Bandwidth sessions awaiting final sample
panels.description: Reporting sessions without a final post-close counter snapshot. Expected while running. Nonzero after completion means unknown tails; zero does not prove telemetry from every Peer was received.

list.name: agent
list.label: Agent
list.description: Select Agents to analyze. This also filters status and resource panels.

list.name: topic
list.label: Topic
list.description: Applies to traffic, window latency, and GRAFT/PRUNE. Session delivery cards use only Run. Peer removal events have no topic.
